description:
Close the arc by deleting the retired direct definition-publication machinery, shrinking scope publication to alias/import/require plus item-macro expansion and compiler callback application, and making the compiler prelude use the real callback path instead of a side channel. Update docs, telemetry, and tests so the staged boundary is explicit and enforceable.

This is the deletion and closeout ticket: remove obsolete reserve/discovery/publication code that only existed to support the parallel direct path, prove the bootstrap floor uses the same model as project code, and restate the invariants clearly.

Signal: there is one compiler definition callback, one scope-shaping expansion model, raw `FunctionSource` stays lazy behind demand, and the remaining `fz-rh2.16.4` work sits above that seam.

comments.text: Reconciliation from fz-rh2.28: the conceptual goals of this ticket — one source read, the bootstrap reads honestly (same model as project code), def-head structure emerges from the define pipeline not a mode-gated re-parse, raw FunctionSource stays lazy behind demand — were delivered by the fz-rh2.28 arc on the current baseline: fz-s00 (delete ScopeSurfaceMode; one reader + canonicalize via build_definition_form), fz-rh2.28.1 (is_bootstrap: the bootstrap is the only canonical-read exception), and fz-rh2.28.3/.4 (env machinery is telemetry-only and removed; __ENV__ is a namespace splice at expansion). This ticket remains blocked by fz-rh2.16.11.5 (old-world ir_codegen/ir_planner rebase parity), which fz-rh2.28 did not touch. Recommend re-scoping fz-rh2.16.11.4 to only whatever direct-publication deletion is NOT already covered by fz-s00 on the rebased baseline, or closing it as superseded once fz-rh2.16.11.5 is resolved. Decision left to the arc owner.

title: Compiler2 definition-macro closeout: delete direct publication, bootstrap honestly, and restate the invariants
